title: Pointer Arithmetic and Bounds
learningObjectives: Describe pointer/reference or lifetime rules involved.
Trace a simple memory access or ownership operation.
Recognize common undefined behavior and safety risks.
Choose a safer approach for a practical task.

understand.concept: Pointer arithmetic is defined within an array object and its one-past-end position. Subtracting pointers is only valid within the same array; out-of-range operations are undefined.
understand.whyItMatters: Pointer traversal can be efficient but is easier to misuse than indexed/container iteration.
understand.explain: Track the originating array and bounds; do not treat arbitrary memory as an array.

examples.title: Pointer step
examples.explanation: Pointer advances two elements within the same array.

examples.title: One-past-end comparison
examples.code: int a[3]{};int* end=a+3;\n// compare with end; do not dereference end
examples.explanation: One-past-end is valid for comparison but not dereference.

examples.title: Pointer difference
examples.explanation: Pointer difference counts elements within the same array.

examples.title: Wrong bounds concept
examples.code: int a[2]{1,2};int* p=a;\n// p+2 is one-past-end; *(p+2) is invalid
examples.explanation: The one-past-end pointer must not be dereferenced.

examples.title: Indexed safer option
examples.explanation: Bounds-checked at() is often easier to reason about than manual pointer math.

practise.guidedTask: Trace the five Pointer Arithmetic and Bounds examples. Mark each pointer/reference's target, object lifetime, mutability and whether dereferencing is valid.
practise.independentTask: Build a small C++ exercise showing pointer arithmetic and bounds. Include safe cases and deliberately describe (but do not execute) one invalid case. Demonstrate how ownership or lifetime is managed.
hints: Draw pointer arrows to live objects.
Use nullptr for empty pointers and check before dereferencing.
Keep pointer arithmetic within one array.
Distinguish pointer constness from pointee constness.
Prefer value returns, containers and smart pointers to manual ownership.

questions.explanation: C++ defines arithmetic within one array bounds.
Subtraction yields difference in elements for same array.
C++ does not guarantee a safe result.
